analysis:
Scope: only .github/workflows/ci.yml. Base lines 529-893 and head lines 1-540 were examined. The rest of the head file, which holds the changed ranges up to about line 1155, was not supplied, so those lines are not covered.

Changed behavior in the visible head:
- Adds SAVE_CACHES, which is true only for pushes to master or dev, and CHECKOUT_SPARSE.
- Adds a repeated block in each job: restore a cached .git, discard it unless git fsck --connectivity-only passes, check out with persist-credentials false, and save .git only when SAVE_CACHES is true.
- Top-level permissions stay at contents: read.
- Actions remain pinned to full commit SHAs.
- Pull requests restore caches but cannot write the .git cache. A cache written by a push to master or dev could therefore poison later PR runs only if that trusted branch were already compromised.
- Leaving credentials out of the saved .git (persist-credentials false) prevents the job token from being cached.
- A restored .git is not verified beyond connectivity, for example its config and hooks. Its writers are limited to trusted pushes, so I found no concrete regression.

Threat-model fit: none of this touches provider runtime, coordinator trust boundaries, attestation, or the KV cache (T-041). New CI attack surface is limited to the cache-poisoning path above, which is trusted-writer only, so I did not report it.

Unverified in the base text: the cluster metadata cache upload step lets a PR save a build cache when it restored nothing (base lines 750 and 755). I saw no head-side change to it. Whether cache entries saved by a PR are isolated from other branches follows from GitHub cache scoping, not from the supplied evidence.

Remaining questions for the next pass:
- Check the unseen head lines 540-1155 for the same .git cache blocks.
- Check that the cluster and provider-ci-build cache saves respect SAVE_CACHES.
- Check the darkbloom-route lanes, which may run on a sandbox runner, for cross-runner cache trust.
